questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Mission Divyastra' test of March 2024:
1. It demonstrated Multiple Independently targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV) technology on an Agni-V missile.
2. Agni-V is a liquid-fuelled missile.
3. MIRV technology allows a missile to carry a single warhead that can be steered towards several targets in sequence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: MIRV means one missile carries several separate warheads, each of which can be directed to a different target, so statement 3 is wrong. Agni-V is a three-stage solid-fuelled missile, which is why it can be launched quickly from a canister; statement 2 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR):
1. Each PCR cycle is carried out at a single constant temperature of about 37 degrees Celsius.
2. Taq polymerase, obtained from Thermus aquaticus, is used because it is not destroyed by the high temperature of the denaturation step.
3. In RT-PCR, viral RNA is first converted into complementary DNA by reverse transcriptase before amplification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A PCR cycle needs three temperature steps (denaturation near 94 degrees, annealing, extension), so a constant 37 degrees is wrong. Taq survives the heat of denaturation, and RT-PCR needs reverse transcriptase to make cDNA from RNA before the usual amplification.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Ch 11; ICMR
questions.h: Taq = Hot-spring bacterium, so the enzyme never melts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's nuclear command structure and doctrine:
1. The Nuclear Command Authority has a Political Council chaired by the Prime Minister and an Executive Council chaired by the National Security Adviser.
2. The Strategic Forces Command, created in 2003, manages the country's strategic nuclear forces.
3. The doctrine rules out any nuclear response to a chemical or biological attack on India or Indian forces.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Political Council is the only body that can authorise use, and the Executive Council gives inputs and carries out its directions. The 2003 doctrine says India retains the option of nuclear retaliation to a major chemical or biological attack, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: PIB, 4 Jan 2003 (CCS review of operationalisation of the doctrine); MEA

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about CRISPR-based genome editing:
1. Cas9 is directed to the target DNA sequence by a guide RNA.
2. Prime editing works by making a double-strand break and then relying on a donor DNA template.
3. Base editors can change one DNA base into another without making a double-strand break.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The guide RNA is what gives Cas9 its address. Both base editing and prime editing avoid a double-strand break (they use a nicking Cas9 fused to a deaminase or a reverse transcriptase), so statement 2 describes ordinary CRISPR repair, not prime editing.
questions.s: Nobel Prize Chemistry 2020 scientific background; Nature Biotechnology reviews

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Missile : Type
1. Astra : Beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile
2. Nag : Third-generation anti-tank guided missile
3. Akash : Surface-to-air missile
4. Nirbhay : Supersonic cruise missile
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Astra, Nag and Akash are correctly matched. Nirbhay is a long-range subsonic cruise missile; the supersonic cruise missile in Indian service is BrahMos.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the production of recombinant human insulin:
1. The first recombinant human insulin (Humulin) was produced in yeast.
2. In the early method, the A and B chains were produced separately in Escherichia coli and then joined by disulphide bonds.
3. The mature insulin in humans retains the C-peptide.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Eli Lilly used E. coli, not yeast, and made the two chains separately before joining them. In the body, pro-insulin loses its C-peptide during maturation, which is why the early method used only the A and B chains.
questions.h: A and B chains + disulphide bridge = insulin; C is cut away.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the BrahMos missile:
1. It uses a solid-propellant booster and a liquid-fuelled ramjet.
2. It has been tested only from land and ship platforms.
3. Its present operational versions fly at hypersonic speeds above Mach 5.
4. Its name is derived from the rivers Brahmaputra and Moskva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: BrahMos is a two-stage missile: a solid booster takes it to supersonic speed and a liquid-fuelled ramjet cruises it at about Mach 2.8. It has also been fired from submarines and Su-30MKI aircraft, and the in-service versions are supersonic, not hypersonic.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about genetically modified (GM) crops in India:
1. Bt cotton is the only GM crop approved for commercial cultivation so far.
2. The Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee functions under the Ministry of Agriculture.
3. In July 2024 the Supreme Court gave a unanimous verdict clearing GM mustard (DMH-11) for cultivation.
4. Bt brinjal was placed under an indefinite moratorium by the Environment Minister in 2010.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The GEAC sits in the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, since GM organisms are regulated under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. The July 2024 judgment in the GM mustard case was a split verdict, after which the Court directed the Centre to frame a national policy on GM crops.
questions.s: Gene Campaign v. Union of India (SC, July 2024); MoEFCC; Ramesh Singh

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of military exercises and partner countries:
1. Nomadic Elephant : Mongolia
2. Dharma Guardian : Japan
3. Ekuverin : Mauritius
4. Mitra Shakti : Bangladesh
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Nomadic Elephant (Mongolia) and Dharma Guardian (Japan) are correct. Ekuverin is with the Maldives and Mitra Shakti is with Sri Lanka.
questions.s: MoD / PIB press releases on bilateral exercises

questions.q:
Match List-I (COVID-19 vaccine) with List-II (technology platform):
List-I
A. Covishield
B. Covaxin
C. ZyCoV-D
D. Corbevax
List-II
1. DNA plasmid vaccine
2. Inactivated whole-virion vaccine
3. Chimpanzee adenoviral vector vaccine
4. Recombinant protein sub-unit vaccine
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Covishield carries the spike gene in a chimpanzee adenovirus (ChAdOx1), Covaxin uses killed whole virus, ZyCoV-D is a plasmid DNA vaccine, and Corbevax uses a recombinant spike receptor-binding protein.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A scramjet-powered vehicle cannot produce thrust from a standstill and needs a booster to reach its operating speed.
Statement-II: A scramjet has no compressor and depends on the forward speed of the vehicle to compress the incoming air before combustion.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A scramjet burns fuel in supersonic airflow, and the only 'compression' comes from the vehicle's own speed through an inlet. Without that speed there is no compression, so a booster is needed first; this is why the DRDO's HSTDV was boosted by a solid rocket motor.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: mRNA vaccines are more stable at room temperature than DNA vaccines and need no cold storage.
Statement-II: mRNA is single-stranded and is quickly degraded by ubiquitous RNase enzymes unless it is protected.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: DNA is chemically more stable, which is why a DNA vaccine such as ZyCoV-D could be stored at a warmer temperature, while mRNA vaccines need cold chains and lipid nanoparticle protection. The second statement is true, but it explains the opposite of what the first claims.
questions.s: Nature Reviews Drug Discovery; ICMR vaccine primers

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS):
1. The CDS exercises operational command over the Army, Navy and Air Force.
2. The CDS is the Secretary of the Department of Military Affairs in the Ministry of Defence.
3. The CDS is the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The CDS is the principal military adviser to the Defence Minister and heads the Department of Military Affairs, but does not hold operational command over the Service Chiefs. Command stays with the Service Chiefs and the Chiefs of Staff Committee, which the CDS chairs permanently.
questions.s: PIB, 24 Dec 2019 (Cabinet decision on CDS and DMA)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety:
1. Its main objective is the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources.
2. It uses an 'advance informed agreement' procedure for the first transboundary movement of living modified organisms meant for intentional introduction into the environment.
3. It was adopted at Nagoya in 2010.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Cartagena (adopted in Montreal in 2000) is about biosafety in the movement of living modified organisms. Benefit sharing and the 2010 adoption at Nagoya belong to the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit Sharing.
questions.h: Cartagena = Cargo of GMOs; Nagoya = Nature's benefit sharing.

questions.q: With reference to India's 'Mission Shakti' anti-satellite test, which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: The target was a live Indian satellite in low Earth orbit.
The interceptor was launched from the Pokhran test range in Rajasthan.
The interceptor was a ballistic missile defence interceptor with a hit-to-kill kinetic vehicle.
India became the fourth country to demonstrate such a capability.
questions.e: The test of 27 March 2019 was launched from the APJ Abdul Kalam Island in Odisha, not Pokhran. The kinetic hit-to-kill kill of the satellite in low Earth orbit made India the fourth country after the USA, Russia and China.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about stem cells:
1. Induced pluripotent stem cells are produced by reprogramming somatic cells with specific transcription factors.
2. The 2012 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to John Gurdon and Shinya Yamanaka for work on cellular reprogramming.
3. Cells of the blastocyst's inner cell mass are totipotent and can form the placenta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Yamanaka's factors turned adult cells back to a pluripotent state, work that Gurdon's nuclear transfer experiments had made thinkable. Inner-cell-mass cells are pluripotent, not totipotent; only the zygote and very early blastomeres can form extra-embryonic tissue such as the placenta.
questions.s: Nobel Prize 2012; NCERT Class XII Biology

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the chronological order in which India became a member:
1. Australia Group
2. Missile Technology Control Regime
3. Wassenaar Arrangement
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: India joined the MTCR in 2016, the Wassenaar Arrangement in 2017 and the Australia Group in 2018. It is still outside the Nuclear Suppliers Group, which is the missing fourth export-control regime.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Microbe / product : Use
1. Streptokinase : Clot buster for patients with heart attack
2. Cyclosporin A : Lowers blood cholesterol
3. Statins (from Trichoderma polysporum) : Immunosuppressant for organ transplants
4. Acetobacter : Conversion of milk into curd
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only streptokinase (from Streptococcus) is correct. Cyclosporin A, from Trichoderma polysporum, is the immunosuppressant, while statins, from Monascus purpureus, lower cholesterol; curd is formed by Lactobacillus, not Acetobacter.
questions.h: Cyclo = 'cycle of transplant'; statin = stay slim in cholesterol.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. INS Vikrant, India's first indigenously built aircraft carrier, was built by Cochin Shipyard Limited.
2. INS Vikrant is propelled by a nuclear reactor.
3. The Kalvari-class submarines are nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Vikrant was built at Cochin Shipyard and commissioned in 2022, but it runs on gas turbines, not nuclear power. The Kalvari class is the Scorpene-design diesel-electric Project 75 line; the nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine is INS Arihant.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about DNA fingerprinting:
1. It is based on the coding regions of genes, which differ widely between individuals.
2. The DNA profile of a person differs from one tissue to another.
3. Monozygotic (identical) twins give the same DNA profile.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Fingerprinting uses repeated non-coding sequences (VNTRs / STRs) that vary in number from person to person. The profile is the same in every tissue of a person, and identical twins, who come from one zygote, share it.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Ch 6 and 11

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about defence procurement and industry in India:
1. iDEX was launched in 2018 to involve start-ups, MSMEs and innovators in defence innovation.
2. Defence industrial corridors have been announced in Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat.
3. In the Defence Acquisition Procedure 2020, the 'Buy (Indian-IDDM)' category has the highest priority.
4. iDEX is funded and managed by the Defence Innovation Organisation, a not-for-profit company set up by HAL and BEL.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The two defence corridors are in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, so statement 2 is wrong. Buy (Indian-IDDM) means Indian-designed, developed and manufactured, which the DAP ranks above Buy (Indian), Buy and Make and Buy (Global).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. BIRAC is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament.
2. The Department of Biotechnology functions under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
3. The BioE3 (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment) policy was approved by the Union Cabinet in August 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: BIRAC was set up in 2012 by DBT as a not-for-profit Section 8 company, not by a statute. DBT sits in the Ministry of Science and Technology, so only the BioE3 statement is correct.

questions.q:
Match List-I (weapon system) with List-II (description):
List-I
A. Pinaka
B. Dhanush
C. K9 Vajra-T
D. Nag
List-II
1. Multi-barrel rocket launcher
2. Indigenous towed howitzer
3. Self-propelled tracked howitzer
4. Anti-tank guided missile
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Pinaka is a rocket artillery system, Dhanush is the towed 155 mm gun made at Gun Carriage Factory Jabalpur, K9 Vajra-T is a tracked self-propelled howitzer, and Nag is a fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile.

questions.q: Dolly, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, was created using the nucleus taken from which of the following?
o: An embryonic stem cell of a lamb
A mammary gland cell of an adult ewe
A fertilised egg (zygote) of a donor ewe
An unfertilised egg of a Scottish Blackface ewe
questions.e: Dolly was made by somatic cell nuclear transfer: a nucleus from a mammary gland cell of an adult Finn Dorset ewe was placed into an enucleated egg of a Scottish Blackface ewe at the Roslin Institute. The egg donor gave the cytoplasm, not the nucleus.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology; Roslin Institute (Nature, 1997)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) radars:
1. The radar beam can be steered electronically without moving the antenna.
2. Each transmit-receive module in the array can generate and receive its own signal, unlike a passive array that feeds a single transmitter.
3. Uttam is an AESA radar developed by DRDO's LRDE for the Tejas fighter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The many small modules of an AESA allow the beam to be steered in a fraction of a second and let the radar track several targets, so a failure of a few modules does not stop it working. Uttam was developed by the Electronics and Radar Development Establishment (LRDE) of DRDO in Bengaluru for the Tejas.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about RNA interference (RNAi):
1. It silences a gene after transcription by targeting its mRNA.
2. It is triggered by single-stranded DNA introduced into the cell.
3. It has been used to develop tobacco plants resistant to the root-knot nematode Meloidogyne incognita.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: RNAi is triggered by double-stranded RNA, which is cut into small fragments that bind and destroy matching mRNA. Plants engineered to make nematode-specific double-stranded RNA silenced the parasite's vital gene when it fed, so the tobacco was protected.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Ch 12; Nobel Prize 2006

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Defence Acquisition Council (DAC):
1. It is chaired by the Defence Minister.
2. It gives the 'Acceptance of Necessity' for capital acquisition proposals.
3. The Prime Minister is a member of the DAC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The DAC is the highest decision-making body of the Ministry of Defence for capital purchases and is chaired by the Raksha Mantri. It clears Acceptance of Necessity, the first formal step; the Prime Minister is not a member (the Cabinet Committee on Security clears large final deals).

questions.q: In hybridoma technology for producing monoclonal antibodies, which of the following cells are fused?
o: A T lymphocyte from an immunised animal and a myeloma cell
A B lymphocyte and a macrophage
A plasma cell and a fibroblast
An antibody-producing B lymphocyte from an immunised animal and a myeloma cell
questions.e: Kohler and Milstein (1975) fused the B cell, which gives the antibody specificity, with an immortal myeloma cell, which gives endless division. The resulting hybridoma grows indefinitely and secretes antibody against a single epitope.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology; Nobel Prize 1984

questions.q:
Which of the following were set up in 2019 as tri-service agencies?
1. Defence Space Agency
2. Defence Cyber Agency
3. Armed Forces Special Operations Division
4. Defence Intelligence Agency
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Government approved the Defence Space Agency, Defence Cyber Agency and Armed Forces Special Operations Division in 2019 to improve joint operations. The Defence Intelligence Agency is older: it was created in 2002 after the Kargil Review Committee's recommendations.
questions.s: PIB / press reports, Jun 2019; Kargil Review Committee follow-up

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about malaria vaccines:
1. The RTS,S vaccine was first recommended by the WHO for children in 2023.
2. The R21/Matrix-M vaccine was developed at the University of Oxford and is manufactured by the Serum Institute of India.
3. Both vaccines target the circumsporozoite protein of Plasmodium falciparum.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: WHO recommended RTS,S in October 2021, and R21 followed in October 2023, so statement 1 reverses the order. Both vaccines target the circumsporozoite protein on the sporozoite stage of P. falciparum, not P. vivax.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's ballistic missile defence (BMD) programme:
1. It is a two-layer system, with Prithvi Air Defence for exo-atmospheric interception and Advanced Air Defence for endo-atmospheric interception.
2. The Akash missile serves as the exo-atmospheric interceptor of the system.
3. The Advanced Air Defence interceptor is designed to engage targets outside the atmosphere.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: PAD works outside the atmosphere and AAD inside it, giving a second chance if the first interception fails; statement 3 reverses this. Akash is a medium-range surface-to-air missile for aircraft and drones and plays no role as an exo-atmospheric interceptor.

questions.q: The Human Genome Project was declared complete in which year?
questions.e: A working draft was announced in 2000, which is the tempting wrong answer, but the project was declared complete in April 2003. The truly gap-free sequence (T2T) came only in 2022.

questions.q: In the context of missiles, the term 'hypersonic' refers to speeds
questions.e: Subsonic is below Mach 1, supersonic is above Mach 1 and hypersonic begins at about five times the speed of sound. Hypersonic vehicles are hard to stop because they combine this speed with in-atmosphere manoeuvring.

questions.q: In 2010, scientists at the J. Craig Venter Institute announced the creation of
o: a bacterial cell controlled by a chemically synthesised genome
the first mammal cloned from an adult cell
the first human embryonic stem cell line
questions.e: They built the genome of Mycoplasma mycoides chemically, transplanted it into a related bacterium, and the cell began replicating under the synthetic genome. It marked the arrival of synthetic biology.
questions.s: J. Craig Venter Institute, Science, May 2010

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Ballistic missile submarines are central to a credible second-strike capability under a no-first-use policy.
Statement-II: Nuclear-powered submarines can stay submerged for long periods, which makes them hard to detect.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A no-first-use state must be able to retaliate after absorbing an attack, which requires a survivable force, so the first statement is true. The second is also true and explains why submarines are survivable, but it does not explain why a no-first-use policy needs a second-strike force.
questions.s: PIB / MEA on Arihant class; Indian Navy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bt toxin in Bt crops:
1. Cry proteins are formed as inactive protoxins that become active in the alkaline gut of the insect larva.
2. The toxin is harmful to humans because the human gut is also alkaline.
3. Bollgard II cotton carries Cry1Ac and Cry2Ab genes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The protoxin is dissolved by the larva's alkaline midgut, activated, and then makes pores in the gut lining, killing the larva. Humans lack the specific gut receptors and have an acidic stomach, so the toxin is not active in us; the second statement is false.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Malabar naval exercise:
1. It began in 1992 as a bilateral exercise between India and the United States.
2. Japan became a permanent participant in 2015.
3. Australia took part in the 2020 edition, making it a four-nation exercise of the Quad countries.
4. France is a permanent participant of Malabar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Malabar grew from an India-US exercise into a four-nation one, with Japan as a permanent member from 2015 and Australia returning in 2020. France holds a separate bilateral naval exercise with India, called Varuna.

questions.q:
Which of the following vaccines contain live attenuated organisms?
1. BCG
2. MMR
3. Inactivated polio vaccine (IPV)
4. Covaxin
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: BCG is a weakened Mycobacterium bovis, and MMR contains weakened measles, mumps and rubella viruses. IPV and Covaxin are inactivated (killed) vaccines, which cannot multiply in the recipient.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Mission Shakti anti-satellite test
2. Pokhran-II nuclear tests
3. Pokhran-I nuclear test
4. Cabinet sanction of the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Pokhran-I came in 1974, the IGMDP was sanctioned in 1983 under Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, Pokhran-II followed in May 1998 and Mission Shakti in March 2019.

questions.q: The 'Positive Indigenisation Lists' notified by the Ministry of Defence are
o: lists of foreign firms allowed 100 per cent FDI in defence
lists of dual-use items whose export needs a licence
lists of weapons that India will export only to friendly countries
lists of defence items that will be bought only from domestic industry after specified dates
questions.e: The first list, in August 2020, had 101 items, with an import embargo applying from stated years. The aim is to create assured demand for Indian industry and cut dependence on imports.

questions.q: The first CRISPR-based gene-editing therapy approved for patients, in 2023, was for the treatment of
questions.e: Casgevy edits the patient's own blood stem cells to switch on foetal haemoglobin, which compensates for faulty adult haemoglobin in both diseases. It was first approved in the UK in November 2023.
questions.s: UK MHRA, Nov 2023; US FDA, Dec 2023

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT part of the original Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP)?
questions.e: The IGMDP, led by Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, covered Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Akash and Nag. BrahMos came later, in 1998, as an India-Russia joint venture.
questions.h: Pa-T-A-A-N: Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Akash, Nag.

questions.q: Azolla, used as a biofertiliser in paddy fields, fixes atmospheric nitrogen through its symbiotic association with
questions.e: Azolla is a floating fern whose leaf cavities house Anabaena azollae, which fixes nitrogen. Rhizobium lives in legume root nodules, Azotobacter is free-living, and Frankia nodulates non-legumes such as Casuarina.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Ch 10; Ramesh Singh

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Tejas fighter and its engine programme:
1. Tejas is a single-engine, tailless, compound delta-wing multirole fighter.
2. Tejas Mk1 is powered by the indigenous Kaveri engine.
3. The Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft is being designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Tejas Mk1 variants fly on the US-made GE F404 engine because the Kaveri engine of GTRE did not reach the thrust needed. The AMCA, the fifth-generation project, comes from the Aeronautical Development Agency of DRDO.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Golden Rice:
1. It has been genetically engineered to produce beta-carotene in the grain.
2. Beta-carotene is converted into vitamin A in the human body.
3. It has been approved for commercial cultivation in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Golden Rice was designed to tackle vitamin A deficiency, which causes night blindness. India has not approved it for cultivation: Bt cotton remains its only GM crop.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology; Ramesh Singh

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about missiles:
1. A ballistic missile is propelled by an air-breathing engine for the whole of its flight.
2. Cruise missiles use aerodynamic lift and fly within the atmosphere.
3. Nirbhay is a long-range subsonic cruise missile.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Ballistic missiles are rocket-powered, burn only in the initial boost phase and then coast on a gravity-governed arc. Cruise missiles stay in the atmosphere using wings and air-breathing engines.

questions.q: In the first clinical gene therapy (1990) for adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency, which approach was used?
o: Functional ADA protein was injected directly into the patient's thymus
Lymphocytes from the patient were grown in culture, a functional ADA cDNA was introduced with a retroviral vector, and the cells were returned to the patient
The defective gene was cut out of embryos using CRISPR-Cas9 before implantation
A donor's bone marrow was transplanted after destroying the patient's immune system
questions.e: Because lymphocytes are short-lived, the treatment needed repeated infusions; a lasting cure would require gene correction in marrow stem cells. CRISPR did not exist in 1990.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about stealth technology:
1. Stealth aims to reduce the radar cross-section through shaping and radar-absorbent materials.
2. A stealth aircraft is undetectable by every type of sensor, including infrared and acoustic ones.
3. Low-frequency radars can detect some stealth aircraft more easily because shaping is optimised against higher radar frequencies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Stealth lowers, but never removes, detectability; infrared heat from engines and acoustic emissions can still be sensed. Shaping that deflects X-band signals works less well against long VHF wavelengths.

questions.q: Bioleaching, used to recover copper from low-grade ores, relies on
questions.e: The bacterium oxidises iron and sulphur compounds in the ore, releasing copper into acidic solution. Methanobacterium makes biogas, and the other two give cyclosporin A and statins.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment; NCERT Class XII Biology

questions.q: The Kalvari-class (Project 75) submarines, based on the Scorpene design, are being built in India by
questions.e: Mazagon Dock builds them under a technology transfer agreement with France's Naval Group. Cochin Shipyard built INS Vikrant, which is the common mix-up.
